$comment: This file is the only description of the backend that this repository is allowed to rely on.
It is a SNAPSHOT, not a live read: platform-backend is a different repository on a different
deploy cadence, and an intern working here has no way to notice that a field was renamed over
there. So the shapes are written down, stamped with the commit they were read from, and a test
asserts the local mock still matches them.
That gives drift a place to show up. It does NOT detect drift on its own - nothing here can
see the other repository. Re-derive it with `npm run contract:derive -- <path-to-platform-backend>`
whenever you touch this feature, and treat a diff as a conversation with the backend owner
rather than a merge conflict to resolve locally.

auth.note: A short-lived HMAC capability token scoped to ONE attempt at ONE booking. The reservation id is taken FROM THE TOKEN; a body value that disagrees is a refusal, not an override. Never put the token in a query string - carrier and proxy logs retain URLs.
auth.dark_when: VENUE_CALL_SECRET unset on the backend. Every route then refuses seam_disabled.

token.hmac: sha256 over "<reservation_id>.<attempt_id>.<expiry_ms>", base64url, key = VENUE_CALL_SECRET as utf8
token.note: Only TWO refusal words, deliberately: an unparseable token, a forged signature and a token for another booking all return invalid, because a refusal that says WHY tells a prober which half of their guess was right.

routes.when: once, in the gap between the carrier answering and the first word
during the call, once per question the opening lines do not already answer
routes.note: `say` is a FINISHED SENTENCE and is always present, including when known is false. `reason` appears only when known is false.

routes.when: during the call, before speaking any deferral

request_body.question_verbatim: string, max 1000, VERBATIM not a paraphrase - optional

routes.note: asked_to_stop_calling is written SYNCHRONOUSLY before this responds. `say` is empty string for answerer_reported - the agent says nothing, it is a report to us.

refusal.why_409: These are not authentication outcomes to retry differently. They mean the call cannot proceed, and the agent's only correct response to every one is to stop before speaking.

known_divergences.what: campaign_not_active is a dead refusal on the deployed backend. It compares campaigns.status against 'archived' and 'deleted', values that column has never held.
known_divergences.mock_default: The mock implements the FIXED behaviour - a paused campaign refuses. Scenario `campaign-paused-today` reproduces the live bug for a regression test.
known_divergences.why: All remaining development is specified against the fixed backend, so the default must be the fixed backend. The bug is reachable on purpose, never by accident.

known_divergences.what: comp_terms is wired to nothing on the deployed backend - the SQL selects NULL::text - so it always returns the honest refusal.
known_divergences.mock_default: Scenario `happy` reproduces today: comp_terms refuses with reason not_agreed. Scenario `comp-known` returns an authored clause, which is what TASK-972 delivers.
known_divergences.why: Both branches must be exercised. Today's is the one on production; tomorrow's is the one being built.
